t: DFS Palindromes: One DFS String + Manacher
o: Key structural fact: dfs(x) appends exactly the concatenation of its children's strings followed by s[x], so every node's string appears as a *contiguous* substring of the root's dfsStr. Therefore we only need to build the root string once (recording each node's [start, end] interval) and test each interval for being a palindrome. Example 1: root string "abaaba" contains "aba" (node 1) and "ab" (node 2) as contiguous blocks. Manacher answers all interval queries in linear time; the naive rebuild-per-node approach is O(n²) and only serves as intuition.
k: Each node's dfsStr is a contiguous substring of the root's dfsStr — build once, query many.
Record [start, end] per node during a single post-order traversal: children consume the cursor sequentially, then s[x] takes one slot.
Manacher on the '#'-separated string checks any substring in O(1): s[a..b] is a palindrome iff p[a+b+1] ≥ b−a+1.

a.n: Approach 1: Rebuild Each Node's String (Brute Force)
a.i: Directly simulate the definition: recursively concatenate children's strings plus s[x], then compare with its reverse. Correct and trivially matches the statement, but total length is O(n²) in the worst case (a path graph), so it TLEs for n = 1e5 — useful only to validate understanding.
s: Build children lists (already in increasing order).
Answer per node: str equals its reverse.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def findAnswer(self, parent: List[int], s: str) -> List[bool]:
        n = len(parent)
        ch = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for i in range(1, n):
            ch[parent[i]].append(i)
        strs = [''] * n
        def dfs(x):
            parts = [dfs(y) for y in ch[x]]
            parts.append(s[x])
            strs[x] = ''.join(parts)
            return strs[x]
        dfs(0)
        return [t == t[::-1] for t in strs]

a.t: O(n²) time and space worst case — each node stores a copy of its subtree string (fails n = 1e5)

a.i: Because node strings are contiguous in the root string, one post-order pass assigns each node an interval [start,end] using a shared cursor. Build the '#'-interleaved string t of length 2n+1 and run Manacher to get radii p. Substring s[a..b] is a palindrome iff p[a+b+1] ≥ b−a+1 — an O(1) check per node.
s: Children lists in increasing order; iterative post-order with a cursor sets start[x] on entry and end[x] after placing s[x].
Construct t = '#s[0]#s[1]#...#' and compute Manacher radii p.
a.t: O(n) — one traversal to assign intervals, one Manacher pass over a 2n+1-length string, O(1) per query
a.sp: O(n) — intervals, Manacher radii, and the interleaved string

w: Always present the brute force first to show you understand the definition, then land on the contiguity observation + Manacher. An alternative optimal route is per-node polynomial hashing (forward and reverse hashes merged over children), but it is fiddlier than Manacher. Pitfalls: children must be processed in increasing index order (they naturally are if built by ascending i), deep trees blowing the recursion stack in Python/JS (use the iterative post-order shown), and the Manacher index formula p[a+b+1] ≥ b−a+1. Follow-ups: answer queries for arbitrary substrings (same Manacher structure), or handle updates to s (palindromic factors / hashing with segment trees).
